planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Oklahoma is a compact, fully double-flowered zinnia series bred for smaller, more numerous blooms on shorter, well-branched plants than giant-flowered types, making it an efficient, high-volume cut-flower series for market growers.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 9-12 inches. Oklahoma is a widely grown cut-flower zinnia series producing small to medium, fully double, dahlia-like blooms about 2-2.5 inches across in a broad range of colors including salmon, scarlet, golden yellow, white, and rose. Compared with giant-flowered series like Benary's Giant or State Fair, Oklahoma plants are shorter and more branching, producing a much higher number of blooms per plant on strong, wiry stems well suited to bunching for market or home cutting gardens. The smaller flower size also makes the series more resistant to weather damage from wind and rain than large dinner-plate-sized zinnia blooms. Deadhead or harvest regularly to encourage continuous branching and flowering from midsummer through frost, and grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the primary disease risk for zinnias in humid climates.

common_name: Cupcake Zinnia (Ruffled Semi-Double Bicolor Cut-Flower Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Cupcake is a semi-double, scabiosa-flowered zinnia mix known for frilly, ruffled center petals in contrasting bicolor combinations, producing unusually textured blooms distinct from flat-petaled zinnia types.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 9-12 inches. Cupcake is a scabiosa-flowered zinnia mix with a distinctive ruffled, cushion-like center of small, tightly packed petals surrounded by a single or semi-double outer ring of larger petals, giving each bloom an unusual layered, textured look often compared to a frosted cupcake. Colors run through mixed pastels and bicolors, with many blooms showing contrasting tones between the outer ring and the ruffled center. Plants are tall and productive, blooming continuously from midsummer through frost with regular deadheading or harvesting, and the unusual flower form makes Cupcake a popular novelty addition to cutting gardens and mixed bouquets alongside more traditional single- and double-flowered zinnia types. Grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the primary disease risk for zinnias in humid climates.

common_name: Polar Bear Zinnia (Giant Pure White Cut-Flower Zinnia)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Polar Bear is a giant-flowered white selection from the Benary's Giant zinnia series, producing large, fully double, pure white blooms on tall, strong stems ideal for cutting and white-themed garden or floral designs.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 12-18 inches. Polar Bear is a giant-flowered white zinnia from the Benary's Giant series, producing large, fully double, dahlia-like blooms 4-5 inches across in a clean, pure white on tall, sturdy stems well suited to cutting. As part of one of the premier cut-flower zinnia series, it shares the group's large flower size, long stem length, and excellent vase life of five to ten days, making it a favorite for white and neutral-toned floral arrangements and weddings. Plants are tall and vigorous, blooming heavily from midsummer through the first frost with regular deadheading or harvesting to encourage continuous production. Grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the primary disease risk for zinnias in humid climates, and stake in windy sites since the large blooms can be top-heavy on the tall stems.

common_name: Sea Shells Zinnia (Unique Rolled Quilled-Petal Zinnia Mix)

planting.note: Direct sow after last frost; Sea Shells is a distinctive zinnia mix whose petals curl and roll lengthwise into tube-like, shell-shaped forms rather than lying flat, giving the blooms a unique, whimsical texture unlike any other common zinnia type.

directions: Sow seeds 0.25 inch deep after last frost; thin to 9-12 inches. Sea Shells is a novelty heirloom zinnia mix distinguished by petals that curl and roll along their length into narrow, tube-like quills rather than lying flat like typical zinnia petals, giving each bloom a distinctive, whimsical, almost fringed appearance often compared to small seashells or curled ribbons. Flowers come in a mix of pink, rose, orange, yellow, and white on plants otherwise similar in size and vigor to standard zinnias. The unusual petal form makes Sea Shells a popular novelty and conversation-piece addition to cutting gardens and mixed bouquets, standing out clearly next to flat-petaled zinnia varieties. Deadhead or harvest regularly to encourage continuous branching and flowering from midsummer through frost, and grow in full sun with good air circulation to reduce powdery mildew, the primary disease risk for zinnias in humid climates.
